## Governance beyond the workspace

Individual protections operate within institutions, markets, and public rules.

Which responsibilities should belong to the researcher, organization, or public authority?


## The data journey

Consider inputs, prompts, uploaded files, generated outputs, tool results, logs, and backups.

Trace which services or people can access each part.


## Different forms of control

| Question | What to establish |
|---|---|
| Rights | Ownership and permitted use |
| Access | Who can view or handle the data |
| Retention | Storage and deletion rules |
| Portability | Export and ability to leave |
| Training | Whether submitted material can be reused |


## Institutional and hosted services

Review the actual service tier and applicable terms.

Document allowed data, access, retention, incident responsibility, and export. A public FAQ is different from a reviewed negotiated contract.


## Local and rented infrastructure

Local inference can increase operational control.

Review model license, connected tools, configuration, provider access, logs, and backups across the complete workflow.


## Feasible protections

Compare protections against your requirements, resources, and unresolved risks.

Self-hosting alone establishes no blanket privacy or ownership guarantee.


## Societal evidence

Separate observed effects, proposed mechanisms, future scenarios, and normative judgments.

Examine source scope, methods, incentives, uncertainty, and disagreement.


## Political agency

The instructor invites a collaborative, interdisciplinary politics suited to the scale of the transformation.

Students can support, qualify, or challenge that position with evidence.


## Proposed reflection

Assess your data flows and a feasible protection strategy.

Explain a societal position, a collective protection you consider necessary, uncertainty, and a serious counterargument.


## Peer discussion

Respond to one or two peers' reasoning or evidence.

Explain whether the exchange changed your view. Board access, privacy, moderation, and submission rules will be set before use.
